purpose: Vigabatrin is used to help control seizures in certain patients. It is specifically approved for adults and children with a difficult-to-treat type of epilepsy called complex partial seizures when other medicines have not worked well enough. It is also used to treat infantile spasms, a serious seizure condition in babies.
how_it_works: Your brain uses a chemical called GABA to help calm down electrical activity and prevent seizures. Vigabatrin works by blocking an enzyme that normally breaks down GABA, so more GABA stays in your brain. With more of this calming chemical available, your brain is better able to keep seizure activity under control.
common_side_effects: Feeling tired or drowsy, dizziness, headache, shaking or tremors, weight gain, swelling in your hands or feet, nausea, memory problems, and irritability. In children, it may also cause sleepiness or excitement.
warnings: Vigabatrin carries a serious risk of causing permanent vision loss, including tunnel vision or even blindness — this can happen even if you feel fine. Because of this, your vision must be checked by an eye doctor before starting and regularly throughout treatment. This medication is only available through a special restricted program called REMS (Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategy). Do not stop taking it suddenly without talking to your doctor, as this can trigger more seizures. Tell your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, as it can harm a baby.
typical_dosing: For adults with complex partial seizures, the usual starting dose is 500 mg twice a day (1,000 mg total per day). Your doctor may slowly increase this to a maximum of 1,500 mg twice a day (3,000 mg total per day) based on how you respond. For infants with infantile spasms, dosing is based on the baby's weight and is determined by the doctor. Always take it exactly as your doctor prescribes.
